## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. The dream and the warning  (`#the-dream-and-the-warning`)

Cited ayat: 12:4-6

> **12:4** إِذْ قَالَ يُوسُفُ لِأَبِيهِ يَٰٓأَبَتِ إِنِّى رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَبًا وَٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِى سَٰجِدِينَ
>
> **12:5** قَالَ يَٰبُنَىَّ لَا تَقْصُصْ رُءْيَاكَ عَلَىٰٓ إِخْوَتِكَ فَيَكِيدُوا۟ لَكَ كَيْدًا إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ عَدُوٌّ مُّبِينٌ
>
> **12:6** وَكَذَٰلِكَ يَجْتَبِيكَ رَبُّكَ وَيُعَلِّمُكَ مِن تَأْوِيلِ ٱلْأَحَادِيثِ وَيُتِمُّ نِعْمَتَهُۥ عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَىٰٓ ءَالِ يَعْقُوبَ كَمَآ أَتَمَّهَا عَلَىٰٓ أَبَوَيْكَ مِن قَبْلُ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسْحَٰقَ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ

### Claims

**c1** (12:4): Yusuf told his father that he had seen eleven stars, and the sun and the moon, and that he had seen them prostrating to him.

**c2** (12:5): His father told him not to relate his dream to his brothers, or they would plot a plot against him, and said that Satan is a clear enemy to the human being.

**c3** (12:6): His father said that in this way his Lord would choose him, teach him the interpretation of events, and complete His favour on him and on the family of Yaqub, as He had completed it before on his forefathers Ibrahim and Ishaq; his Lord is knowing and wise.

### One-minute summary

Yusuf told his father that he had seen eleven stars, the sun and the moon prostrating to him [c1]. His father told him not to tell his brothers, and said that his Lord would choose him and complete His favour on him [c2][c3].

### Complete story

Yusuf told his father that he had seen eleven stars, and the sun and the moon, and that he had seen them prostrating to him [c1].

His father told him not to relate his dream to his brothers, or they would plot a plot against him, and said that Satan is a clear enemy to the human being [c2]. He said that in this way his Lord would choose him, teach him the interpretation of events, and complete His favour on him and on the family of Yaqub, as He had completed it before on his forefathers Ibrahim and Ishaq [c3].

### Deep study

The passage is a short exchange: the dream [c1], the warning to keep it from the brothers [c2], and the father's words about what his Lord would do [c3]. The dream is given as seen and told, and the verses do not interpret it here [c1]. The father names the forefathers on whom God had completed His favour [c3].

### Kids mode

Yusuf told his father about a dream in which eleven stars, the sun and the moon bowed down to him [c1]. His father told him not to tell his brothers [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the father answers the dream with care for his son and with trust in God's choosing [c2][c3]. Another is that the warning names Satan as a clear enemy to the human being [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: how old Yusuf was when he saw the dream, or where the family lived in this passage.
- Not established: the meaning of the dream in this passage; Yusuf speaks of its interpretation later in the surah (12:100), which is outside this record.
- Not established: how the brothers learned of the dream, or whether they did.
- The Quran says the stars were eleven; it does not say what they stood for. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: identifications of the stars, the sun and the moon with named persons; none is used here.
